issues: The reasonable inference that the multitude remains fallen while crying is not explicit in verse 2, which describes their earlier falling in verse 1; show the fallen posture only if continuity from the preceding verse is intended.
“They” and “their” are supported by the preceding verse’s multitude, though this scene labels them “the people.”
The verse says the Spirit of the Lord came upon them but does not describe a visible appearance; the scene correctly leaves that unspecified.

The factual and quotation content is supported by Mosiah 4:24–25. The scene does not specify a setting or the appearance of the addressed poor; keep these visually unspecified. The first-person words are explicitly instructed as words to say in their hearts, not an additional spoken exchange.
The preceding scene is consistent in chronology: it covers Benjamin’s prior warning to the rich (Mosiah 4:22–23), while this scene moves to his next address to the poor (Mosiah 4:24–25).
